newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Rio Grande state to restructure power companies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Rio Grande state to restructure power companies.

text.p: Brazil's southern state of Rio Grande do Sul has announced a plan to restructure its power companies and privatize five of them within eight months.

"The bill to restructure our power sector is expected to be approved by the Assembly by the end of this month. We hope to hire consultants to advise us in January. I think within eight months we will start selling off some companies," a Rio Grande do Sul state government spokeswoman told Reuters.

Under the plan, the government will privatize its gas company Sulgas and split its electrical power company Companhia Estadual de Energia Eletrica (CEEE) into six firms, which will be controlled by a holding company.

Three of the six -- a thermoelectric plant and two power distributors -- will be auctioned off. The other three, which include a hydroelectric plant, an electric grid company and a distributor will remain with the state, she said.
The state may also sell a minority stake in the holding company, to be named CEEE, in the future, she added.
The spokeswoman said the restructuring will allow CEEE to pay off part of its debts to the federal government and allow private investors to produce electricity in the state.
Currently, CEEE buys 70 percent of the energy it produces reach 1.8 billion reais ($1.74 billion) this year.
In addition, the plan calls for the restructuring of the state's mining company Companhia Riograndense de Mineracao (CRM), which produces 35 percent of all coal in Brazil.
The spokeswoman said the government plans to auction off concessions to manage and explore the company's two existing mines.
